business_problem: AIA needed to support a broad technology, digital, and analytics transformation across Asia-Pacific, but private-data-center operations, fragmented service tools, and slow back-office processes limited the speed, scale, and user experience it wanted to achieve.
solution_summary: AIA used ServiceNow IT Service Management and IT Operations Management as the foundation for its cloud-driven transformation. As the insurer migrated 86% of its environment to the public cloud, those platforms became the self-service interface where developers and internal IT teams assemble solution building blocks without waiting on low-level infrastructure work. ITSM and ITOM also synchronize technology services and operations on one cloud platform so employees can access tools more easily and lines of business can work from a more agile, secure, and automated operating model. That shift mattered at scale: AIA was dealing with spikes such as a 400% increase in processing demand across 17 platforms handling 1.3 billion records a day, while simultaneously expanding staff training through its internal cloud academy. ServiceNow effectively became the primary window through which employees access the digital environment that underpins AIA's growth strategy.

data_flow: Developers and internal IT teams access self-service building blocks through ServiceNow as AIA's cloud platforms deliver services behind the scenes. ITSM and ITOM coordinate service delivery, automation, and operational context so business lines can access digital capabilities from one primary workflow window instead of fragmented tools.
business_outcome: AIA automated close to 70% of back-office activities, supported a 400% increase in processing demand on workloads handling 1.3 billion records daily, completed 86% of its public-cloud transition by 2022, and generated multimillion-dollar cost savings while improving digital employee experience.
